title: Kitchen Notice Standards for the Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
The production kitchens of Larkspur Table work to the notice printed against each service level of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement. Three notice figures and one surcharge are printed against every level.

**Standard notice** is the notice an ordinary order needs before service, in whole hours. **Shortest accepted notice** is the shortest notice at which an order is still taken at all. **Rush surcharge** is the surcharge carried by an order placed inside the standard notice, as a percentage of order value. **Dietary notice** is the notice needed before service to build allergen and dietary meals into an order, in whole hours.

| Service level | Standard notice (hours) | Shortest accepted notice (hours) | Rush surcharge | Dietary notice (hours) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop-Off Catering Account | 24 | 4 | 12.0 per cent | 24 |
| Delivered Buffet Account | 48 | 8 | 15.0 per cent | 24 |
| Attended Buffet Account | 72 | 16 | 18.0 per cent | 48 |
| Staffed Full-Service Catering Account | 96 | 24 | 22.0 per cent | 48 |
| Executive Hospitality Catering Account | 72 | 12 | 25.0 per cent | 24 |
| Campus Catering Master Account | 120 | 36 | 20.0 per cent | 72 |

The rush surcharge rises with the service level rather than with the length of the notice window: the Executive Hospitality Catering Account carries the highest rush surcharge in the schedule at 25.0 per cent although its standard notice of 72 hours is shorter than the 96 hours of the Staffed Full-Service Catering Account.

Dietary notice and standard notice are separate figures and are not always equal. On the Attended Buffet Account the two coincide at 48 hours; on the Campus Catering Master Account dietary notice of 72 hours is shorter than the standard notice of 120 hours; on the Executive Hospitality Catering Account dietary notice of 24 hours is a third of the standard notice.
